title: Air-fryer rump steak
subtitle: A well-rested rump steak cooked to order in the air fryer.
excerpt: Rump steak seasoned with salt and cooked in a preheated air fryer for a medium-rare finish with a darkened crust. Cheaper than sirloin or ribeye, with more flavour when cooked right. Serves two.
sourceNotes: Rump steak is a well-worked cut from the hindquarter, cheaper than sirloin but with more beefy flavour. The air fryer circulates hot air at high temperature and works as a dry-heat cooking method, producing a Maillard-browned exterior when the steak is dry-seasoned before cooking.

content.text: Rump steak in the air fryer produces a good crust with minimal effort. Bring the steak to room temperature before cooking so the centre doesn't stay cold when the exterior browns. Pat completely dry, season generously with salt, and preheat the fryer before the steak goes in.
Cook times for doneness at 220°C with a 2.5 cm steak: rare 8 minutes total, medium-rare 10 minutes, medium 12 minutes. Use a thermometer if uncertain: 52°C rare, 57°C medium-rare, 63°C medium.

items.prepNote: two steaks, about 2.5 cm thick, at room temperature

content.text: Remove the {{beef-rump}} steaks from the fridge 30 minutes before cooking. Pat dry and brush both sides with {{olive-oil}} of olive oil. Season well with {{sea-salt-flakes}} of flaked salt and cracked black pepper. Preheat the air fryer to 220°C for 3 minutes. Cook the steaks for 5 minutes, flip, and cook for a further 4-7 minutes to your preferred doneness. Rest on a warm plate for 5 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: Crust pale and grey, no browning
items.cause: Steak not patted dry, or fryer not preheated.
items.fix: Dry the surface thoroughly. Brown only happens on a dry surface at high heat. Always preheat the fryer.
Rest at room temperature for at least 30 minutes before cooking. A cold centre means the outside overcooks before the middle warms through.
Rump has more connective tissue than sirloin. It's best at rare to medium-rare. Past medium it toughens noticeably.
Expected at high heat. Empty the drip tray before cooking and ensure the kitchen is ventilated.

content.text: Rump steak is the everyday steak: more flavour than sirloin, less tender, and a third of the price of fillet. Good with chips, a green salad, or a simple peppercorn sauce. Slice against the grain to shorten the muscle fibres and improve the texture.
